cards.teach:
Compressor: evens out loud and quiet notes and adds sustain.

Where it goes: Early in the chain, usually before the gain pedals.

Used for: Country and funk chicken-pickin, smooth clean tones, longer sustain on solos.

Try this: Turn Sustain up and pick softly, then hard. Notice the quiet notes bloom and the loud ones get squashed.

Play with it in Library → Pedals.

cards.teach:
Clean Boost: makes your signal louder without changing the tone much.

Where it goes: Before an amp or drive pedal, or at the end for a solo lift.

Used for: Solo volume jumps, pushing a tube amp or another pedal harder.

Try this: Switch it on and off: same notes, just more level. Great stacked in front of a drive pedal.

Play with it in Library → Pedals.

Fuzz: turns the signal into a thick, fizzy, almost square-wave buzz.

Where it goes: Often first in the chain (fuzz likes your guitar directly).

Used for: Psychedelic, garage and stoner rock. Big, woolly sustain.

Try this: Roll your guitar volume down and the fuzz cleans up. Try Fuzz on max for a wall of buzz.

Play with it in Library → Pedals.

Compressors go early so they feed your gain pedals an even signal.

cards.teach:
Wah shapes the raw tone, so it sits before time-based effects like delay.

Common order: tuner → wah → compressor → drive/fuzz → modulation (chorus, phaser…) → delay → reverb. Rules of thumb, not laws.
cards.why: Wah shapes the raw tone, so it sits before time-based effects like delay.

f.p: In a typical pedal chain, which comes earlier: wah or delay?

cards.teach:
Gain first, then modulation, so the chorus swirls the distorted sound rather than being distorted itself.

Common order: tuner → wah → compressor → drive/fuzz → modulation (chorus, phaser…) → delay → reverb. Rules of thumb, not laws.
cards.why: Gain first, then modulation, so the chorus swirls the distorted sound rather than being distorted itself.

f.p: In a typical pedal chain, which comes earlier: overdrive or chorus?

cards.teach:
Modulation before delay keeps each echo clean instead of re-modulating them messily.

Common order: tuner → wah → compressor → drive/fuzz → modulation (chorus, phaser…) → delay → reverb. Rules of thumb, not laws.
cards.why: Modulation before delay keeps each echo clean instead of re-modulating them messily.

f.p: In a typical pedal chain, which comes earlier: chorus or delay?

cards.teach:
Reverb last puts the echoes inside the same space.

Common order: tuner → wah → compressor → drive/fuzz → modulation (chorus, phaser…) → delay → reverb. Rules of thumb, not laws.
cards.why: Reverb last puts the echoes inside the same space.

f.p: In a typical pedal chain, which comes earlier: delay or reverb?

cards.teach:
Fuzz likes to be near the guitar; reverb goes at the end.

Common order: tuner → wah → compressor → drive/fuzz → modulation (chorus, phaser…) → delay → reverb. Rules of thumb, not laws.
cards.why: Fuzz likes to be near the guitar; reverb goes at the end.

f.p: In a typical pedal chain, which comes earlier: fuzz or reverb?

cards.teach:
Phasers sound smoother after distortion than before it.

Common order: tuner → wah → compressor → drive/fuzz → modulation (chorus, phaser…) → delay → reverb. Rules of thumb, not laws.
cards.why: Phasers sound smoother after distortion than before it.
